model_and_data: Reanalysis of non-neural experiments from Belkin et al., cited as BHMM19. The located tree experiment varies the maximum number of terminal leaves and then an ensemble of trees; once the ensemble count exceeds one, the extract calls the model a random forest without bootstrapping. The located boosting experiment uses trees with 10 leaves as base learners. Main-text results use MNIST with ntrain = 10000. A separate linear-regression experiment is also located.
loss: Squared loss. The extract says the reanalyzed methods are trained by minimizing the squared loss. In multi-class settings it attributes to BHMM19 a one-vs-rest strategy that reports squared loss summed across classes. The footnote digit printed immediately after 'squared loss' on that protocol line is not part of the loss name.
varied_axis: Two raw-parameter routes, used both as separate sweeps and as a composite sequence. For trees, the maximum allowed number of terminal leaf nodes P leaf is increased, and the number of trees P ens is increased. The composite curve transitions from increasing P leaf with P ens = 1 to increasing P ens with P leaf = n. For gradient boosting, the number of boosting rounds P boost is increased and then the number of independent models P ens is increased. The extract says a double-descent shape occurs where the method of increasing complexity switches.
held_fixed_axes: The training objective in this setup is squared loss. Tree sweeps fix P ens while varying P leaf, or fix P leaf while varying P ens. Boosting sweeps are described as a U- or L-shape in P boost for a fixed number of ensemble members, and an L-shape in P ens for fixed boosting rounds. The located boosting replication uses trees with 10 leaves and learning rate gamma = 0.85, as printed with the Greek letter in the extract. The main-text sample is MNIST with ntrain = 10000.
interpolation_definition: Two printed forms are located. Page 1 says the second-descent location is not inherently tied to the interpolation threshold, and the next line begins p=n. Page 4 says the interpolation threshold p = n plays a special role only on the P leaf axis, where it determines maximal depth, while P ens can be increased indefinitely. For a single tree, P leaf cannot be increased past n, described as every leaf containing only one instance. In the boosting experiment, P boost is increased until the squared training error reaches approximately zero, after which P boost is fixed. The extract does not supply a separate formula identifying that approximate-zero training error with p = n.
assumptions: The reanalyzed machine-learning methods are trained by minimizing squared loss.
The multi-class protocol attributed to BHMM19 is one-vs-rest squared loss summed across classes.
Main-text results use MNIST with ntrain = 10000.
A single tree cannot increase P leaf past n, when every leaf contains only one instance, and larger leaves may already be pure.
When P ens > 1 the plotted model is an ensemble of trees, a random forest without bootstrapping.
The boosting replication uses trees with 10 leaves and learning rate gamma = 0.85.
That boosting experiment increases P boost until squared training error is approximately zero, then fixes P boost and increases P ens.
The interpolation threshold is printed both as p=n and as p = n, and on the P leaf axis it determines maximal depth.
result_type: Empirical reanalysis of the located tree, boosting, and linear-regression plots. For the tree and boosting plots, the extract reports classical convex shapes on each separate axis and a double-descent shape only at the switch from one way of increasing raw parameter count to the other. This is a report about those plots.
transfer_limits: The located loss is squared loss, including one-vs-rest squared loss summed across classes. CatBoost and logloss are absent from this extract. The tree and boosting intervention switches between P leaf or P boost and P ens, so these plots do not document a split-candidate sweep with ensemble size held fixed. The linear-regression experiment is identified as a separate case from the tree and boosting experiments.
